content:
Quick start

nfprogress does not store the text of the manuscript, but its measurable progress. The basic unit of work is the project; A large project can be broken down into stages.

  1. Open the Projects section and click Create Project. In the legacy version of PySide6, Ctrl+N is also available for this.
  2. Indicate the name, final goal, value already achieved and unit of measurement. If necessary, select a deadline, daily goal, stages and streaks.
  3. Select a project from the list. In the “New Entry” field, enter new general meaning, not the number written since the last entry. The application will calculate the difference itself.
  4. Keep track of your progress, your cumulative goal for today, and your recording history. In Tauri desktop, a project can be linked to local Word or Scrivener; Web and mobile versions accept an explicitly selected Word .docx file.
  5. Game mode is enabled separately in the settings. It adds rewards, character, store, quests and Creative Rhythm, but does not change project data.

Important: the daily project goal and the game goal of the day in “Creative Rhythm” are different mechanisms. The first helps to meet the deadline and supports the streak; the second is a daily challenge for an in-game reward.
title: Quick start

children.content:
List, search and navigation

  • Click a project or milestone to open its details, entries, and action buttons.
  • The arrow of a project opens or collapses its stages. You can drag and drop stages within a project to change their order.
  • The search finds both projects and milestones. Double-clicking a found stage clears the search, expands its parent project, and selects the stage from the normal list.
  • The filter switches between active, archived and completed projects. The stages are shown along with the parent.
  • Sorting by deadline places projects without a deadline separately; sorting by progress uses the overall percentage complete. The selected filter and sorting of the new interface are saved separately so as not to change the legacy version list settings.

The last selected project or stage is remembered and opened the next time you start it.
children.title: List, Search, and Navigation

children.content:
Creating a project

  1. Click "Create Project" on the Projects tab or select "Project → Create Project".
  2. Enter a unique non-empty name.
  3. Set a positive final goal and a non-negative current amount. This allows you to start tracking the text already written.
  4. Select a unit: characters, A4 sheets, author's sheets, or Fikbook pages. The calculations use the ratios: 1 A4 sheet = 1,800 characters, 1 author's sheet = 40,000 characters, 1 Fikbook page = 4,500 characters.
  5. Specify a deadline or check "None." The date cannot be earlier than the current writing day.
  6. Enable streak and auto-freeze if necessary. These elements are visible only with the appropriate settings.
  7. To break down the work, enable "staged project" and add stages before saving or after creating the project.

The deadline and the "Goal for the day" field are linked: changing one recalculates the other. Before saving, the form shows the first detected error.
children.title: Creating a Project

children.content:
Project stages

Stage — a nested project with its own name, goal, current value, records, deadline, daily plan, streak, and synchronization. All stages use the unit of measurement of the parent project.

  • Create a stage using the «Add Stage» button in the project form or the «Project → Create Stage» item after selecting a project with stages.
  • The overall goal and volume of the parent are equal to the sum of the goals and volumes of the stages; the parent fields become read-only.
  • If the parent does not have a deadline, its displayed goal for today is the sum of the daily goals of the stages. If the parent has a deadline, the overall plan is calculated for the sum of the stages.
  • When adding a deadline to the parent, the longest streak of the stage is transferred to the project, and the stage streaks are cleared. Their deadlines are retained.
  • Converting a regular project into a staged one transfers the history, progress, and synchronization to the first stage. The reverse conversion merges records by time and recalculates the overall progress.
  • A stage cannot be archived, but it can be modified, completed, or deleted separately. Completing the entire project also completes all unfinished stages.

In a "General Project," stages are used as independent synchronization sources and have unlimited goals.
children.title: Project stages

children.content:
Project and Stage Maps

Every project and stage has its own independent idea map. Select the project or stage on the “Projects” tab and click “Map” in the action panel. The editor opens in a separate window; the root node is named after the project or stage when the map is first opened.

  • Double-click a node or press Space to edit its text. Tab adds a child node, Enter adds a sibling, and Delete removes the selected node.
  • “Free node” creates a first-level node outside automatic layout; its children look like second-level nodes. Regular shortcuts, the context menu, links, and Summary all work. The context menu or drag-and-drop can detach a regular branch with all its children or attach a free branch to a map node. Notes also support editing, deletion, links, and Tab for a nearby note.
  • Nodes can be dragged. The context menu adds, links, moves, and groups nodes, while the built-in toolbar controls zoom and centering.
  • The focus mode button on the bottom toolbar displays the selected first-level branch separately. Press it again to return to the combined map.
  • The search icon on the top toolbar or Ctrl+F (Command+F on macOS) searches regular and free nodes as well as notes. Select a result to expand its branch, select the item, and center it on the map.
  • Changes are saved automatically with the project data. The “Save” button and closing the window also store the map’s current state.
  • The Export button saves the current map as PNG, SVG or JSON. PNG and SVG are suitable for viewing and sharing, while JSON stores the editable map structure.
  • In the edit window for a staged project, you can enable “Combine stage maps in the project map”. Each stage will then appear in the combined map as a separate first-level branch under its current name.
  • Branch content is synchronized both ways: changes in the combined map are saved to the individual stage maps, and changes to an individual map appear the next time the combined map is opened. The project’s own nodes are preserved.
  • Renaming, adding, deleting, and reordering stages is automatically reflected in the combined map. Turning off combining only hides the generated branches and does not delete stage maps.
  • A completed stage is marked with ✅ in the combined map. Its existing map and its branch in the combined map are read-only. If no stage map was created, the “Map” button shows a message, and the combined map displays the same explanation in the bottom status area rather than as a separate node. A completed project map is also read-only.
  • Deleting a project or stage also deletes its map. When a staged project is converted to a regular project, maps belonging to the removed stages are not merged into the parent map.

The editor and its resources are bundled with the application, so an internet connection is not required to use the map.
children.title: Project and Stage Maps

children.content:
Project Notes

Select a project or milestone and click the separate Notes button in the action bar. A single space of cards will open: here are the regular notes of the selected entity and the floating notes of its mind map. A parent project with milestones first shows only its own notes.

  • “New Note” opens the editor with the cursor in the text; a new map node is not created. Clicking on the card opens the same editor. Changes are saved automatically, closing with the “Done” button, Escape or clicking on the background.
  • The title is optional. The color covers the entire editor. "Done" is on the same page as palette, archive, and delete; a filled pin means pinning.
  • Standard Ctrl/⌘ combinations work. For a link, select the text and enter the address: with another action, the correct address is saved. Tags are entered separated by commas, become chips and filter cards when pressed.
  • In the parent project, the Stage Notes button separately includes cards for all stages. Each of them has a noticeable mark “Stage: …”. The adjacent menu selects one stage, and the By Stage switch groups the order of cards by stage.
  • The search takes into account the title, text, checklist items, tags and stage name. While “Stage Notes” is turned off, the search only works for notes from the project itself; once enabled, it covers the stages as well. The tags menu allows you to quickly filter cards; system tag #карта only shows Mind Map notes.
  • Card #карта associated with the Mind Elixir stable element identifier. Changing its text changes the same note on the map, and creating, editing or deleting it on the map is immediately reflected among the cards.
  • System tag #карта cannot be deleted. Text formatting is not available for this card because Mind Elixir's native format stores the note as plain text. An individual card title can be changed; this does not change the name of the card element.
  • The Open on Map action opens the map, selects the associated note, and displays it in the center. Removing a card #карта requires confirmation and only deletes the associated note, not other map nodes.
  • The archive hides the card from the main list without deleting it; The “Archive” switch shows and allows you to restore such notes. Cards are arranged in order of addition in a responsive grid. Dragging the special handle changes the order, and after releasing the card always occupies a grid cell.

The note editor and grid library are included in the application and do not require an Internet connection. In a completed project or phase, notes are viewable only; the same restriction applies to cards of completed stages in the general window of the parent project.
children.title: Project Notes

children.content:
Progress and records

In the "New record" field, enter the current total quantity in the chosen unit. For example, if it was 12,000 characters and became 13,500, enter 13,500: the record will save the change +1,500.

  • Click "Save" or Enter. The same value as the previous one does not create a record.
  • An increase creates a positive entry; a decrease — a negative one. The project percentage is calculated as the current amount divided by the goal.
  • Game rewards and character-count challenges progress only with a positive difference. An active session with the “Edit text” intention also counts text reductions by the absolute change.
  • The history shows the date and time, the change, the new total, and the contribution to the project percentage. A milestone project shows the milestone name next to it.
  • Deleting a selected entry is irreversible. After deletion, the current amount is taken from the last remaining entry, and if the history is empty, it becomes zero.

Synchronization automatically creates the same entries. The writing day start time from the settings determines to which day an early entry belongs.
children.title: Progress and Records

children.content:
Deadlines and daily goals

The deadline is included in the calculation as a full-time working day. The remaining volume is divided by the number of days from today to the deadline inclusive. In the form, you can change the date and get a new daily rate, or change the rate and get a new date.

The card shows savings goal for today: how much should be in the project by the end of the current writing day. To find out the amount of work remaining for today, compare this mark with the current amount. The missed volume does not disappear - the next cumulative mark continues the plan.

  • When a deadline is reached or passed, the cumulative goal becomes equal to the full project goal.
  • Changing a goal, deadline, unit, milestones, or personal daily rate restructures the future plan, preserving past days and taking into account what has already been written today.
  • In the project or stage change window, you can check “Recalculate daily goals from today” as long as the daily goal does not change. Then today’s plan will start from the current progress, and the deadline will move along the remaining volume.
  • Removing a deadline resets the daily goal. When a streak is active, the application will warn you about its loss.
  • When streaks are enabled, you cannot reduce the daily goal before completing the current one. Increasing an already completed goal may require extending today's streak again; A repeat game reward for the same day will not be issued.

“Start time of day” in the settings shifts the border of the day. For example, if you start at 04:00, the entry at 02:00 refers to the previous writing day.
children.title: Deadlines and daily goal

children.content:
Streaks and frosts

First enable Streaks in the settings, then allow streaks in a specific project or stage. A local streak begins or extends when the current quantity reaches that day's cumulative goal.

  • The global streak is extended if the daily goal is met in at least one active streak source.
  • Statuses show whether the streak has started, was renewed today, is awaiting renewal, frozen, lost or completed along with the project.
  • In the new interface, the global streak is located above the list of projects. The project's streak is shown when the parent's deadline; if the parent does not have a deadline, their own streaks are shown on the tiles of stages with deadlines and inside the open stage.
  • The Freeze item covers one missed day of a suitable local or global streak. Autofreeze uses the item automatically if the condition has not yet been met and freezing is allowed.
  • Archiving a project removes its deadline and interrupts the streak. Disabling an entity's streak clears its current streak.
  • Disabling the global Streaks setting clears local and global streaks across all projects and phases.

In game mode, starting, continuing and completing streaks provide rewards. Losing a global streak causes damage to the character; successfully applied freezing prevents this loss.
children.title: Streaks and Freezes

children.content:
Sync with Word and Scrivener

In Tauri desktop, set up local source in the "Word and Scrivener" section. Subsequently, the application reads the new number of characters, compares it with the current progress and creates a record with the difference. Web, iOS and Android do not get arbitrary persistent access to the file system: there, select and download the .docx file explicitly.

  • Word: select the .docx file. The old .doc format is not supported - save the document as .docx. The text of paragraphs and tables is counted.
  • Scrivener: Only in Tauri desktop, select the local .scriv project, then a specific text document, chapter or scene. Remote and mobile clients do not upload the Scrivener project to the server.
  • For active desktop bindings, launching the selected source and synchronizing all sources are available; background synchronization only works when the desktop setting is enabled.
  • Decreasing the outer text creates a negative entry. There is no in-game reward given for it.
  • For a project with stages, each stage has its own binding, and synchronizing the parent sequentially updates all active linked stages.
  • “Delete synchronization” removes the link, but saves the already created entries and progress.

For direct synchronization, the ramp time and source stability are checked. If a file, folder, or Scrivener item is inaccessible, out of date, corrupted, or changed during reading, a new entry is not created and the binding is retained. Choose a new path or unbind manually when you really need it.
children.title: Synchronization

children.content:
Statistics and publication of progress

After selecting a project, open its statistics. It is calculated from the saved history: number of records, total volume, average values ​​for active days and records, used freezes, best day and day of the week, current and maximum streaks, duration of work and other indicators.

For a project with stages, statistics are built according to the combined chronology of all stages.

The Share button for a final project or milestone creates a 1080×1080 square PNG card with the title and current percentage. For a milestone, both the project and the milestone are listed in the title.

The Share menu contains separate actions: the copy icon writes the card to the clipboard, and the save icon starts downloading the PNG. If the clipboard is not available, the application does not automatically replace the download action; manuscript text, notes and other data are not sent to an external service.

For the infinite "General Project" and its sources, the card is not available because they do not have an end goal and percentage of completion.
children.title: Statistics and Publishing

children.content:
Edit, archive, complete, and delete

  • Edit: allows updating the name, goal, current value, unit, deadline, daily goal, streak, and structure of stages. Changing the unit irreversibly converts goals, entries, and progress with the intended rounding.
  • To archive: available only for top-level projects. The deadline is removed, the streak is interrupted, and the project moves to the "Archived" filter. It can be reactivated, but the deadline will need to be set again.
  • Complete: available after reaching the final goal. The action is irreversible; a completed entity can be viewed or deleted, but cannot continue to be edited. Completing the parent completes unfinished stages.
  • Delete: permanently deletes the project or the selected stage along with its history. If the last stage is deleted, the parent becomes a regular project.

Game rewards for completion are given once. The stage reward is a quarter of the reward for an independent project of the same size.
children.title: Editing and Statuses

content:
Projects and stages

The project combines a goal, current volume, progress records, deadline, daily plan, status and, with streak mode enabled, its own series of productive days.

A typical project is tracked as a whole. A project with stages serves as a container: its goal, scope and progress are made up of stages, and records are shown in a general chronology with the names of the stages.

Three statuses are available for work: active, archived and completed. The filter above the list determines which status is shown; sorting sorts projects by title, deadline or progress, and in the new interface also by recent changes.
title: Projects and Stages

content:
Application Settings

  • Endless Project: creates a “General Project” without an end goal. It is suitable for small unrelated texts and multiple synchronization sources. Disabling the setting deletes the “Shared Project” along with the data accumulated in it, but first creates a backup copy of the data files and settings in the folder backups.
  • Game mode: Shows or hides the game tab. Hiding does not reset a saved character.
  • Streaks: includes a global mechanism and allows you to customize project streaks. Disabling clears the history of the current local and global series; A backup copy is also created before such a reset.
  • Show how much has been written today: displays the total result of the current writing day for all projects. In the new interface, this card is located above the list of projects.
  • Notification display time: sets the duration of pop-up messages in the legacy version and the new interface; the valid range is from 1 to 3600 seconds. Saved bank and streak events are opened using the “Notifications” button, remain in history and are marked as read separately.
  • Start time of day: defines the writing day boundary for entries, daily goals, and streaks.
  • Language: immediately switches between Russian, English, Spanish, German, French or Brazilian Portuguese interface.
  • Interface animation: Full animation makes changes to pie charts and progress bars noticeable; Same as System mode follows the operating system's motion reduction setting, and Reduced turns off decorative motion.
  • Check for updates: manually starts a new version check only in the legacy version of PySide6. The Tauri update will appear after the release of signed Tauri packages.

In Vue/Tauri/Ionic, settings are opened through a separate “Settings” section; in the legacy version - through the menu “Settings → Application settings”.
title: Application Settings

children.content:
Rewards, levels, and health

  • Basically, every 100 added characters give 10 coins and 500 experience. The total is multiplied by the character's parameters, inspiration, effects, specialization, and relics.
  • Negative entries do not take away previously awarded rewards, but they also do not give new ones.
  • When leveling up, the character receives coins, fully restores health, and gains 2 skill points per new level.
  • Maximum health starts at 100 and increases by 10 every five levels.
  • Prices and some monetary rewards take inflation into account: its multiplier increases by 15% for each level after the first.
  • Starting, extending, and completing streaks give separate rewards. Losing a global streak deals 5 units of damage for each lost day of the series.
  • At zero health, an available resurrection potion is automatically used or offered for purchase. Without resurrection, the character returns to level 1, loses all experience and inventory, and half of the coins.

Completing a project provides a one-time reward depending on its volume; completing a stage uses a 25% coefficient.
children.title: Rewards, levels, and health

children.content:
Character parameters and skills

On the parameters tab, coin, experience, and health recovery multipliers are shown. Select a row to see the actual effect of the multiplier considering level, skills, and active items.

  • Productivity adds +0.25 to the experience multiplier for each invested point.
  • Profitability adds +0.25 to the coin multiplier per point.
  • Endurance restores an additional 0.25 health per hour per point.

2 points are awarded for each new level. Increase the value of the desired skill with the counter; confirmed points cannot be removed or transferred to another skill.

Temporary buffs, debuffs, and permanent item effects are added on top of the base multipliers. Lists show the parameter, amount, number of additions, and remaining time.
children.title: Parameters and Skills

children.content:
Store and inventory

The store is divided into items, potions and rewards. Product availability varies by tier; the card shows price, description, effect and quantity limits.

  • Select the product, quantity and click “Buy”. If there are not enough coins, a credit for the missing amount may be offered for an authorized product from level 3.
  • The prices of most built-in products rise with inflation. Some items have stock limits or are one-of-a-kind items.
  • Inventory can be filtered by type; the selected type is saved for the new interface. The consumable item is used with the “Use” button; The permanent effect of the equipment lasts as long as the item is in the inventory.
  • Allowed items are sold for 75% of the current price. Quest rewards and some unique items cannot be sold.
  • “Freeze” is used through a separate selection of a suitable project or global streak.

In the reward store, you can create a personal reward: set the name, price and inflation effect. It does not provide a gaming effect - purchase and use serve as a promise of real reward. Personal rewards can be changed and deleted.
children.title: Shop and inventory

children.content:
Quests, buffs, and debuffs

Quests unlock by level and are divided into available, active, and completed.

  1. Select an available quest, read the condition and reward, and click "Take Quest."
  2. Fulfill the condition in projects or game mode. The app periodically checks only active quests and automatically completes those that meet the requirements.
  3. You can decline an active quest: it will return to the available list and lose the dates of the current attempt.

The reward may include coins, experience, items, and buffs. A completed quest remains in the history and cannot be repeated.

Buffs increase stats, debuffs decrease them. The effect card shows the source, change coefficient, magnitude, and duration. Temporary effects disappear after expiration; compatible stackable effects show the quantity and total.
children.title: Quests, buffs, and debuffs

children.content:
Bank

The bank is opened with a button in the character block. It shows your credit score, limit, daily rates and estimated income. The rating depends on the level, expected income from text and streaks, property, deposits and credit history.

  • Credit Available from level 3, only one at a time and within the limit. The first payment is due the next day. If the balance is sufficient, the daily payment is debited automatically; Manual, partial and full payment are also available.
  • A missed payment after the end of the day adds a penalty of 1.5% of the balance, but not less than 5 coins, causes 10 damage and worsens the rating.
  • Contribution debits the selected amount and capitalizes the interest daily. It can be replenished. The option with withdrawal of accumulated interest allows you to withdraw it once a day; refusing this opportunity ups the ante.
  • Closing the deposit early returns the principal amount, but burns the interest. After the deadline, the principal amount and remaining income are returned.

There can be one loan and one deposit at the same time. Banking events are also saved in the Notifications center: you can read them one at a time or mark them all at once without losing your history.
children.title: Bank

content:
Game mode

Game mode turns actual work on text into character development. It is enabled in the settings and accounts for positive entries of regular projects, stages, and synchronized sources.

Coins and experience are awarded for text, streaks, project completions, challenges, sessions, and manuscript milestones. Coins are spent in the shop and bank, experience increases the level, and inspiration controls the functions of the “Creative Rhythm”.

Game data is saved separately from projects. Disabling the mode hides the tab, but does not delete the character, inventory, or achievements.
title: Game mode

children.content:
Inspiration and abilities

1 inspiration is awarded for every 500 characters added. It is also given for successful sessions, challenges, milestones, and certain items. The maximum is 100; relics can increase the actual award.

The current reserve passively increases text rewards from 0% to 10%. Inspiration can be spent on one of the pending effects:

  • Creative Impulse — 30: +25% coins and experience for the next positive entry.
  • Session Spark — 25: +25% to the next successful writing session.
  • Challenge Focus — 40: +25% to the next completed daily or weekly challenge.

The same effect cannot be activated a second time while it is pending application. The session bonus is not spent on failure, while focus is until the actual completion of the trial.
children.title: Inspiration and abilities

children.content:
Daily in-game goal

At the beginning of each writing day, three sentences of different types and complexities are created. The first is selected automatically; the other can be chosen before completion for 15 inspiration.

  • Daily volume: write the specified number of characters. The base is 80% of the average result of productive days over the previous 14 days, rounded to the nearest hundred and limited to the range of 500–5,000. If there is no story, the base is 1,000.
  • Session rhythm: complete 1–3 successful writing sessions.
  • Editor’s day: complete 1–2 successful sessions with the intention “Edit text”.

Difficulty “Easy”, “Normal”, or “Hard” changes the goal and reward. After completion, coins, experience, and 10 inspiration points are awarded. “Challenge Focus,” the Explorer bonus, and relics increase coins and experience.

Completed goals cannot be changed. A new day creates a new set and resets unfinished progress. The “new goal token” switches to the next option for free.

Do not confuse: this is a game challenge, not a cumulative project goal by deadline.
children.title: Daily Game Challenge

children.content:
Weekly challenges

Select one challenge for the current week:

  • Marathon: 10,000 characters; reward 500 coins and 1,500 XP.
  • Rhythm: positive entries on 4 different days; 400 coins and 1,200 XP.
  • Clean Flow: 5 successful writing sessions; 450 coins and 1,350 XP.
  • Editorial Week: 3 successful sessions with the intent to edit; 425 coins and 1,300 experience.

Upon completion, an additional 20 inspiration is awarded. 'Trial Focus', the Researcher specialization, and relics multiply coins and experience.

In the usual way, the selected trial does not change and remains until next Monday, even after completion. The active skill of the Researcher replaces it with the next option but resets progress. With the start of a new week, the old trial is removed.
children.title: Weekly challenges

children.content:
Writing sessions

Select a mode, intention, duration of 15, 25, 45, or 60 minutes, and a positive goal in characters. In a regular session, only added text increases progress. With the “Edit text” intention, the absolute change in total length is counted: an entry of +500 or −500 adds 500 processed characters.

  • Sprint: only 15 minutes, +15% to the reward.
  • Flow: free mode without an additional multiplier.
  • Deep work: only 45 or 60 minutes, +25%.
  • Editorial pass: requires the intention "Edit text", +20%.

The application determines the edited amount from the difference between the previous and new total. Rewording text without changing the total length cannot be detected automatically and does not create a progress entry.

Click "Finish" to lock in the result: bronze — 100% of the goal, silver — 125%, gold — 150%. Success gives a base of 25 coins with inflation, 250 experience, and 10 inspiration, then mode, rank, streak, specialization, and other bonuses are applied. Silver or gold, completed before the timer ends, get an additional +10%.

Failure does not give a reward and resets the streak unless it was protected. Canceling does not count as a result and does not affect the streak. The timer does not automatically end a session; it uses real time and continues between launches.

Each consecutive success adds +3% to the reward, up to a maximum of +15%. The last 20 results are stored; a short history is available in the status tooltip.
children.title: Writing sessions

children.content:
Specializations and mastery

Specializations unlock at level 3. After choosing, changing direction is only possible after 14 days. The passive bonus increases by 2.5 percentage points for each new mastery rank; ranks are achieved at 0, 3, 8, 15, and 25 mastery experience.

  • Marathoner: from +15% for entries of at least 3,000 characters; such an entry provides mastery experience.
  • Ritualist: from +25% for successful sessions; each success gives mastery experience.
  • Finisher: from +20% for completing stages and projects; mastery comes from milestones and completions.
  • Explorer: from +20% for daily and weekly challenges; completed challenges give mastery.
  • Editor: from +25% for successful sessions with the intention to edit; they also develop mastery.

"Mastery Textbook" adds 2 experience points to the current specialization. Experience in different specializations is stored separately and retained after switching.
children.title: Specializations and Mastery

children.content:
Active specialization skills

A skill can be activated once every 24 hours. The pending effect remains until the appropriate event occurs; new use is unavailable until then.

  • Long Breath: +30% to the next entry of at least 3,000 characters.
  • Ritual Power: +30% to the next successful session; if the next completed session fails, instead of the bonus, it preserves the streak once.
  • Rush to the Finale: +30% to the next new milestones of a manuscript, reached by a single entry.
  • New Route: Immediately replaces the active unfinished weekly challenge with the next one and resets its progress.
  • Precise Gaze: +30% to the next successful editor session.

The recovery countdown begins only after successful activation. An unsuitable record or session does not consume the pending effect.
children.title: Active specialization skills

children.content:
Creative events

Each individual positive entry of at least 1,000 characters is considered a productive action. After five such actions, one pending event appears. Until it is resolved, nothing new is created.

When an event is pending, select an option from the list and click Resolve Event. “Safe Choice” always gives the specified reward, while “Take a Risk” offers an increased reward with a 55% chance of success. The exact outcome of the selected option is shown in a tooltip.

  • Unexpected idea: guaranteed 6 inspirations; risk - 15 inspiration or loss 5.
  • Second Wind: guaranteed +10% to the next entry; risk - +30% or loss of 8 inspiration.
  • Lucky Find: guaranteed 50 coins; risk - 150 coins or nothing.

The event does not open the modal window while writing text. It waits for a decision on the “Creative Rhythm” tab, is applied exactly once and then goes into the history of the last 20 events.
children.title: Creative Events

children.content:
Manuscript path

The final project or stage receives one-time rewards for milestones reached for the first time. If a single entry skips over several boundaries, all missed rewards are issued:

  • 10% "Spark of Idea": 25 coins, 250 experience, 2 inspirations.
  • 25% "First Chapters": 50 coins, 500 experience, 3 inspiration.
  • 50% "Turning Point": 100 coins, 1,000 experience, 5 inspiration.
  • 75% "Home Stretch": 150 coins, 1,500 experience, 7 inspiration.
  • 90% "Almost Done": 200 coins, 2,000 experience, 8 inspiration.
  • 100% "Manuscript Completed": 300 coins, 3,000 experience, 10 inspiration.

Coins scale with inflation; specialization, items, and relics can multiply coins and experience. Each step's path is saved separately. Renaming carries over the achieved milestones to the new name, so there is no repeat reward. Infinite projects have no milestones.
children.title: Manuscript path

children.content:
Cabinet, relics and kits

The Cabinet is located on the right side of the game mode, on the “Cabinet” tab next to the “Inventory” tab.

Relics are opened automatically along the boundaries of different manuscripts. A locked relic hides the name and description, but shows the condition and progress.

  • 10% of one text: “Ink Candle”, +1% per written text.
  • 50% of one text: “Map of plot twists”, +3% for tests.
  • 100% of one text: “Binding of the first manuscript”, +5% for completions.
  • 25% of three texts: “First Chapter Shelf”, +3% for successful sessions.
  • 75% of one text: “Tipping Point Pen”, +5% abroad.
  • 90% of one text: “Finish line lamp”, +10% to inspiration received.
  • 50% of three texts: “Atlas of Three Worlds”, +2% for written text.
  • 100% of three texts: “Shelf of completed manuscripts”, +10% for completions.

The “Path of the Great Manuscript” set of five relics of one full path adds +3% to all coins and experience rewards. An “Author's Library” of three multi-project relics increases inspiration received by 20%. The effects of relics and open sets stack.
children.title: Cabinet, Relics, and Sets

children.content:
Items of creative rhythm

  • Potions and sparks of inspiration restore the specified supply up to the maximum.
  • Inkwell of the flow adds +25% to the next successful session; the effect remains upon failure.
  • Manuscript compass adds +25% to the next new milestones achieved by a single entry.
  • Mastery tutorial gives 2 experience to the selected specialization.
  • New goal token chooses the next option of an as-yet-uncompleted daily game goal for free.
  • Ritual thread saves a series once during an unsuccessful completed session; up to three defenses can be prepared.
  • Quality Medal increases the next successful bronze or silver session by one rank; only one can be prepared at a time.

The item is written off only after successful use. If the condition is currently unattainable or the effect limit has been reached, it remains in the inventory.
children.title: Creative Rhythm Items

content:
Creative Rhythm

"Creative Rhythm" is a large set of motivational mechanics within the game mode: inspiration, daily game goal, weekly challenge, writing sessions, specialization, creative events, and the manuscript path.

All mechanics progress with real application events. Symbolic goals receive only the positive difference of a new entry; session goals—only a successfully completed session; editorial goals—a successful session with the intention "Edit text." In such a session, progress is the absolute change in length: both additions and reductions count.

State is saved between launches. Daily prompts change with the new writing day, the weekly challenge changes on Monday, and an active writing session continues to count real time even when the application is closed.
title: Creative rhythm

content:
Hotkeys

In Vue/Tauri/Ionic, actions are performed by visible buttons and form elements. In open help, Ctrl+F or Command+F turns focus to its search; standard browser and system combinations remain available.

The following combinations apply to the legacy version of PySide6 desktop:

  • Ctrl+H — open this help window.
  • Ctrl+N - create a project.
  • Ctrl+S — synchronize the selected project.
  • Ctrl+E — change the selected project or stage.
  • Delete — delete the selected project or stage.
  • Ctrl+Shift+S — open statistics of the selected project.
  • Ctrl+Shift+H — archive or activate the selected project.
  • Ctrl+Shift+C — complete the selected project or stage.

For standard New and Save commands, legacy macOS can show system options with Command. The combination for opening help in the legacy version remains Ctrl+H.
title: Hotkeys
